confirmed.element: ?state=seam — .peel, "THE WORDS YOU PICKED" block above the .peelField labelled "THE TASK WORDING"
confirmed.problem: The centrepiece of the most important cross-product moment in the suite prints the same sentence twice, 40px apart, at identical type: picked reads "Switch on before guests arrive, not when." at 17px/600, wording reads "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" at 17px/600. The only difference is a full stop. A stranger cannot tell why both exist or which one crosses. Worse, the second one is the only editable object in the seam and it is a textarea with 0px border and transparent background at rest, so its editability appears only after you have already clicked it. The panel is 266px wide beside 660px of empty white on the writing side.
confirmed.fix:
Keep both objects, stop setting them identically, and give the seam its one real field.

1. Make the wording a field at rest, not on click: `.peelField` gets `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line-strong)` (rgba(17,17,17,0.16), an existing ink tint), `background: var(--white)`, `border-radius: var(--r-chip)` to match the `.picker` beside it, and padding to match; `:hover` steps the inset to `var(--ink-2)`-weight the way `.act:hover` already does. Legal inside the three-colour lock; no new hue, no new weight.

2. Break the type collision the old gate caused, without demoting the person's words. The two must not both be 17/600 in a 266px column. Either set `.peelFrom span` at 17/400 so the provenance reads as the quoted source and the field reads as the live object, or keep 17/600 on the provenance and let the field's new fill and rule carry the distinction — but not both identical and both flat. Re-point the "the person's words outrank the machine's version" assertion at rank rather than raw fontSize (order in the DOM plus tint), so the gate stops forcing the collision it was written to prevent.

3. Collapse the tinted block while it is still a clone. At rest, when the field value equals the pick modulo case and terminal punctuation, print the provenance as one quiet 12px line ("From your note", or reuse the existing sourceLabel string) rather than a second 17/600 restatement of the sentence already highlighted in the note 380px away. The moment the wording is edited away from the pick, restore the full tinted block — that is when it earns its area, and it is the only moment a person needs to compare.

4. Take the width from the sheet, never from the measure. The plane is capped at 1000px inside a 1322px sheet: 322px unused. When a peel is open, let the two-column grid use it — writing column stays at its 527px measure, margin goes from 266px to ~380px. Do not touch `--measure`.

Copy stays notes-copy.ts's own; do not invent "The task will say" or "Edit this and the note stays exactly as you wrote it" without routing them through the copy file and the brand-voice check.
confirmed.done: Same fix.

confirmed.element: .undo strip in ?state=notebook and ?state=review; the review deck note "every decision can be put back"; the delete sheet in ?state=not-yet
confirmed.problem: Reversibility has an undeclared 10-second fuse. Measured: the strip lives 9.9s after a capture and 9.8s after a hand decision, then disappears; pressing Ctrl+Z after that changes nothing and announces nothing (row count and "2 of 8" both unchanged, live region still reading the old message). The review screen states "Nothing is decided until you say so, and every decision can be put back" with no time bound, and the product's own delete sheet promises "You can undo this for thirty seconds" while the live delete in the hand gives ten. Three different truths about the same guarantee, and the keyboard route dead-ends in silence.
confirmed.fix: Honour one number and declare it where the promise is made. Set `offerUndo`'s timer to 30000 so the live window matches the thirty seconds the delete sheet already promises, and make the delete window read from the same constant rather than a second hardcoded value. Give the deck line the bound it is missing so the sentence stops outliving the affordance. Drop the ink-density countdown from the proposed fix: a pill that visibly decays for thirty seconds reads as a rendering fault, not as a clock, and none of the named benchmarks does it. Keep the keyboard repair — when Ctrl+Z arrives outside the capture field with an empty undo slot, `doUndo` should `say("Nothing left to undo.")` and preventDefault rather than returning false into silence. Separately worth noting, and arguably the larger half of the same defect: `undone` is a single slot, so after two decisions in the hand the deck reads "2 decided just now, and every one of them can be put back" while only the second is recoverable — I drove it and the first Ctrl+Z took 3 of 8 back to 2 of 8 and the second did nothing at all. Whatever the window becomes, that sentence is false as long as the stack holds one act.
confirmed.done: Same fix: the window is declared on the strip itself.

confirmed.element: ?state=review · press T (or click "Send to Tasks" on the hand card) → .peel / .peelField / .peel [data-act="send"]
confirmed.problem: The hand's peel is the product's most important moment and it is the worst-written one. Driven live: pressing T announces "Highlight the words you want in the note first." — the product's only scolding imperative, fired as a greeting at a state that is not an error. The panel it opens does not ask anything: .peelField has aria-labelledby="peel-label" ("The task wording") and placeholder="", so it is a labelled empty box with no question in it. Its primary reads "Send to Tasks" at full ink, disabled=false, opacity 1 — and clicking it with the field empty does nothing at all: peel still open, no inline message, and the aria-live region still holds the same stale sentence, so it does not re-announce and a screen-reader user gets silence. Meanwhile a second, identically worded "Send to Tasks" stays fully enabled on the card behind (two buttons, same four words, different jobs, both opacity 1). The claimed round-4 fixes — the peel "asks", the primary "states its precondition at rest", the note's action row "stands down" — all hold on the desk seam and none of them hold in the hand.
confirmed.fix: Mirror the desk in the hand, and fix the primary once for both. (1) T with nothing picked should invite, not scold: replace N.copy.nothingSelected on this route with the desk's own grammar, e.g. "Nothing picked yet. Write what the task should say, or pick the words in the note." (2) Put the ask where the eye already goes: when pickedWords is null, render the question in the slot the seam gives to "The words you picked" — "What should the task say?" as the peel's label line — and give .peelField a matching placeholder so the ask survives after the label scrolls out of the reading path. Do not let a placeholder be the only carrier. (3) Change the peel primary in peelPanel (not just in the hand) to state its precondition at rest — "Write the wording, then send" while taskWording is empty, swapping to "Send to Tasks" the moment the field has content. Leave it enabled and focusable; the point is that it never refuses after a press, and this also closes the same silent no-op on the seam. (4) Do not aria-hide the card's action row with tabindex -1 — a container hidden from AT with focusable children is the anti-pattern, and it is not what the desk does. Do exactly what readSheet does: while peeling, replace .handFoot's contents with the stood-down line ("Writing the task below.") plus the escape back, so precisely one "Send to Tasks" is live on screen, no control is invisible-but-focusable, and the T key stays guarded as it already is.
confirmed.done: The product's only scolding imperative is gone from its most important flow. The peel invites: nothing picked yet, write what the task should say or pick words in the note. The field carries the question as its placeholder, and the primary says Write the wording, then send until there is wording.

confirmed.element: notebook.js:900 — .act [data-act="timeline"] "Send to Timeline", beside the primary on every opened note
confirmed.problem: The product's second promise is a sealed one-way edge: only the exact words a person picks ever cross, and the note never leaves. Immediately beside it, one press from the primary and styled in the same button family, sits "Send to Timeline": one click, no boundary sentence, no picking step, no statement of what crosses, no confirmation grammar. The words never say whether the note leaves. A promise that holds for one destination and is silent for the destination next to it is not a promise, and it is the one place in the file where the copy contradicts the product's central claim by omission.

Do NOT build the first branch — a second full peel with its own boundary sentence and confirmation would state the same promise twice in two near-identical margin panels, on a Timeline contract that does not exist anywhere in data.js. confirmed.element: notebook.js applyDraft() → the `${draft.length} / 4000` textContent write, fired from the input handler via setTimeout(…,0); .topField / .phoneField
confirmed.problem: The headline claim — "one Ctrl+Z gives back the whole typing burst" — is false at human typing speed. Typed at 12/40/90ms per key, one Ctrl+Z in the capture field returns exactly ONE character; it takes 32 presses to clear a 33-character burst. A bare textarea injected into the same page returns the whole burst in one press, and .peelField (no per-keystroke DOM write) returns its whole burst too, so this is the file's own doing, not the browser's. Deferring by a tick does not save the undo group: applyDraft still writes the counter's textContent between every keystroke, and Chromium ends the typing-undo unit on any script mutation of the document. The interaction gate certifies the opposite only because it types at 0ms delay, which batches keystrokes ahead of the deferred write, and then asserts the weak `after.length < 40` on a 51-character string. In a capture product, undo returning one letter is the most expensive defect on the sheet.
confirmed.fix: Stop mutating the document while a burst is in flight, on BOTH capture surfaces. Preferred: delete the live counter entirely -- remove the `${draft.length} / 4000` span from notebook.js:94 and :801 and the `.dockCount` span from :708, and delete the whole `for (const node of mount.querySelectorAll(".topMeta[data-count], .dockCount"))` textContent loop at notebook.js:104-106. The 4000 denominator is never enforced anywhere in the file, so nothing is lost. If the count must survive, gate that loop behind 500ms of keyboard idle (raise the inputTimer delay to 500 for the count-only path) so no mutation can land inside a burst; leave the one-shot data-live toggle alone, since it fires only on the first character, before a burst has anything to lose. Then fix the gate so it can never certify this again: at scripts/design/notes-interaction-check.mjs:1198 type with { delay: 40 } and assert the field is EMPTY after one Ctrl+Z, not merely under 40 characters; add the identical assertion at 390x844 against .phoneField, since the dock path fails the same way. If the counter is deleted, also remove the now-dead "the counter counts" / "and keeps counting" assertions at notes-interaction-check.mjs:534 and :538.
confirmed.done: The round-4 fix only worked at machine speed. At 40 to 90ms a key a setTimeout(0) lands BETWEEN keystrokes, so the document was still being mutated inside the browser's typing history. The write waits for a 450ms pause now, and the one thing that cannot wait — the sheet waking — is a custom property on the root that changes no node at all. The gate types at 40ms and at 90ms and fails on anything less than a burst.
